facts.text: George Washington surveyed and platted the town of Washington, Virginia, in July 1749, making it the first town named after him.
The town’s streets honor the first landowners—Jett, Wheeler, Porter, and Calvert—who helped lay its grid.
In 1975, Washington’s core was listed as the Washington Historic District on both the Virginia Landmarks Register and the National Register of Historic Places.
The opening of The Inn at Little Washington in 1978 turned the town into a culinary destination recognized worldwide.
The Rappahannock County Courthouse, built 1834‑35, showcases Jeffersonian architecture with its two‑story Flemish‑bond brickwork.
Washington became the county seat of Rappahannock County in 1833, anchoring its role in regional governance.
